message.content:
Let each of the two equal piles have \(x\) pins.

So John originally had:

\[
2x
\]

He gave away one-half of one-third of one pile:

\[
\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{3} \times x = \frac{x}{6}
\]

He had 66 pins left, so:

\[
2x - \frac{x}{6} = 66
\]

\[
\frac{12x}{6} - \frac{x}{6} = 66
\]

\[
\frac{11x}{6} = 66
\]

\[
11x = 396
\]

\[
x = 36
\]

Originally, John had:

\[
2x = 72
\]

The answer is 72.
